raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

#62956 routes unquantized BF16 linear layers and LM heads through the shape-dynamic CuTe DSL skinny GEMM when `skinny_gemm_plans.py` has a measured plan for the device, the local `(N, K)` and the token count. SM90 has no plans, so on H100 / H200 every dense decode GEMM still goes to cuBLAS, which reads the weight at 2.3-3.7 TB/s at 1-4 tokens.

This PR adds `SM90_SKINNY_GEMM_PLANS` for the TP=1 local shapes of Qwen3-4B / 8B / 14B / 32B and Llama-3.1-8B (QKV, o_proj, fused gate/up, down, LM head), registered under capability `(9, 0)`. No code path changes: shapes or token counts without a plan keep using cuBLAS.

## Claims

- **E2E, H200, one request:** median TPOT -14.9% on Qwen3-8B (6.02 -> 5.12 ms), -12.5% on Qwen3-4B, -11.0% on Llama-3.1-8B, -10.5% on Qwen3-14B, -12.7% on Qwen3-32B (20.24 -> 17.68 ms). Two concurrent requests: -8.3% to -12.2%. Four: -5.4% on Qwen3-8B, -3.9% on Qwen3-32B, -2.3% on Qwen3-14B, within run-to-run spread on Qwen3-4B and Llama-3.1-8B. Eight: unchanged (batch > 4 stays on cuBLAS).
- **`Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (BF16 MoE, `torch.compile`), added after the first review round:** three dense cells (fused QKV `(5120, 2048)`, o_proj `(2048, 4096)`, LM head `(151936, 2048)`): median TPOT -5.5% at one request (4.755 -> 4.493 ms), -2.6% at 2, about -3% at 4, unchanged at 8 (no plan).
- **Accuracy:** GSM8K 5-shot on Qwen3-8B (1319 questions, greedy, 2 concurrent requests so decode runs the planned kernels): 0.8886 without, 0.8893 with the plans.
- **Kernels:** 52 cells, each 1.07x-1.61x faster than cuBLAS with the weight read from HBM. A cell is listed only when it also wins with a hot L2 and, for 4 tokens, inside a running model (see Details).

## Validation

### Per-cell GEMM time

H200 NVL, vLLM nightly `0.33.0rc1.dev421` with #62956 applied, BF16, CUDA graph replay, the weight rotated over enough copies that every call reads it from HBM, and each GEMM preceded by a small non-PDL elementwise kernel (as in the model; its time is subtracted). Median of 7 paired repeats, cuBLAS -> plan in us:

| projection | (N, K) | M=1 | M=2 | M=4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-4B QKV | (6144, 2560) | 12.0 → 8.8 (1.37x) | 12.9 → 9.3 (1.39x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-4B gate/up | (19456, 2560) | 32.3 → 23.9 (1.35x) | 32.4 → 24.3 (1.33x) | 32.4 → 29.0 (1.12x) |
| Qwen3-4B LM head | (151936, 2560) | 193.5 → 178.6 (1.08x) | 194.1 → 180.4 (1.08x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-4B o_proj | (2560, 4096) | 11.1 → 6.9 (1.61x) | 11.2 → 7.7 (1.45x) | 11.0 → 8.7 (1.26x) |
| Qwen3-4B down | (2560, 9728) | 19.6 → 13.2 (1.48x) | 19.5 → 13.8 (1.41x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-8B / Llama-3.1-8B o_proj | (4096, 4096) | 14.9 → 9.6 (1.55x) | 14.8 → 10.4 (1.42x) | 14.7 → 11.4 (1.30x) |
| Qwen3-8B / Llama-3.1-8B QKV | (6144, 4096) | 18.7 → 13.0 (1.43x) | 17.5 → 13.8 (1.28x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-8B gate/up | (24576, 4096) | 57.8 → 48.4 (1.20x) | 58.1 → 49.4 (1.18x) | 58.4 → 52.6 (1.11x) |
| Qwen3-8B LM head | (151936, 4096) | 309.8 → 281.5 (1.10x) | 310.6 → 284.4 (1.09x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-8B down | (4096, 12288) | 32.8 → 24.4 (1.35x) | 33.0 → 25.9 (1.27x) | 33.3 → 27.8 (1.20x) |
| Llama-3.1-8B gate/up | (28672, 4096) | 61.0 → 55.9 (1.09x) | 59.7 → 57.3 (1.04x) | cuBLAS |
| Llama-3.1-8B LM head | (128256, 4096) | 257.0 → 238.2 (1.08x) | 257.0 → 241.0 (1.07x) | cuBLAS |
| Llama-3.1-8B down | (4096, 14336) | 34.5 → 28.0 (1.23x) | 34.5 → 29.3 (1.18x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-14B o_proj | (5120, 5120) | 18.0 → 14.0 (1.28x) | 17.4 → 14.2 (1.22x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-14B QKV | (7168, 5120) | 25.4 → 17.6 (1.44x) | 24.9 → 19.4 (1.29x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-14B gate/up | (34816, 5120) | 92.2 → 82.7 (1.11x) | 93.3 → 85.2 (1.09x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-14B / 32B LM head | (151936, 5120) | 384.7 → 351.3 (1.10x) | 385.3 → 354.2 (1.09x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-14B down | (5120, 17408) | 55.1 → 42.6 (1.29x) | 54.8 → 42.9 (1.28x) | 55.2 → 47.5 (1.16x) |
| Qwen3-32B QKV | (10240, 5120) | 30.9 → 24.9 (1.24x) | 30.8 → 26.0 (1.19x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-32B gate/up | (51200, 5120) | 140.0 → 121.4 (1.15x) | 140.1 → 123.0 (1.14x) | cuBLAS |
| Qwen3-32B o_proj | (5120, 8192) | 28.7 → 20.1 (1.43x) | 29.1 → 21.1 (1.38x) | 29.3 → 24.5 (1.20x) |
| Qwen3-32B down | (5120, 25600) | 74.4 → 62.8 (1.18x) | 74.0 → 63.1 (1.17x) | 74.1 → 68.5 (1.08x) |

Kept: >= 5% faster with a cold L2 and >= 3% faster with a hot L2 (single weight copy), plus the in-model check below for 4 tokens. cuBLAS cells did not pass. At 8 and 16 tokens the skinny GEMM loses on every shape (0.4-0.9x), so no plans are listed there.

### E2E

H200 NVL, TP=1, `vllm serve <model> --max-model-len 4096 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --seed 0`; 32 prompts at concurrency 1, 8x the concurrency otherwise. Both arms run the same nightly image with #62956's files applied; the PR arm adds this plan file. `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1` in both arms (see Details). Two runs per arm, interleaved on two GPUs with the GPUs swapped. Median TPOT (ms), both runs:

| model | conc. | without plans | with plans | change |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | 6.010 / 6.022 | 5.128 / 5.116 | -14.9% |
| | 2 | 6.105 / 6.050 | 5.350 / 5.325 | -12.2% |
| | 4 | 6.178 / 6.183 | 5.843 / 5.845 | -5.4% |
| | 8 | 6.402 / 6.395 | 6.396 / 6.396 | 0 |
| Qwen3-4B | 1 | 4.049 / 4.052 | 3.547 / 3.541 | -12.5% |
| | 2 | 4.119 / 4.125 | 3.674 / 3.666 | -11.0% |
| | 4 | 4.258 / 4.267 | 4.260 / 4.245 | 0 |
| | 8 | 4.450 / 4.458 | 4.462 / 4.449 | 0 |
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | 1 | 5.421 / 5.345 | 4.794 / 4.787 | -11.0% |
| | 2 | 5.487 / 5.440 | 5.012 / 5.008 | -8.3% |
| | 4 | 5.554 / 5.511 | 5.448 / 5.494 | -1.1% |
| | 8 | 5.737 / 5.738 | 5.730 / 5.815 | within spread |
| Qwen3-14B | 1 | 9.346 / 9.364 | 8.382 / 8.370 | -10.5% |
| | 2 | 9.575 / 9.584 | 8.659 / 8.651 | -9.7% |
| | 4 | 9.603 / 9.629 | 9.401 / 9.390 | -2.3% |
| | 8 | 10.025 / 9.909 | 10.038 / 9.860 | within spread |
| Qwen3-32B | 1 | 20.227 / 20.255 | 17.668 / 17.693 | -12.7% |
| | 2 | 20.598 / 20.621 | 18.241 / 18.262 | -11.4% |
| | 4 | 20.634 / 20.697 | 19.874 / 19.841 | -3.9% |
| | 8 | 21.137 / 21.183 | 21.191 / 21.548 | within spread (output tok/s 326.5 / 326.0 -> 325.9 / 325.9) |

Output throughput moves with TPOT (Qwen3-8B at concurrency 1: 162.7 -> 190.2 tok/s). TTFT is unchanged within run-to-run spread.

`Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B` (BF16), same setup, four launches on one GPU in the order base, PR, PR, base; the routed experts run the Triton fused MoE in both arms, the plans only cover the dense projections and the LM head:

| conc. | without | with this PR | change |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 1 | 4.755 / 4.755 | 4.493 / 4.493 | -5.5% |
| 2 | 5.514 / 5.512 | 5.370 / 5.370 | -2.6% |
| 4 | 6.941 / 6.669 | 6.728 / 6.565 | -2% to -3% |
| 8 | 8.670 / 8.353 | 8.356 / 8.631 | 0 (no plan) |

Per-cell (H200, cold L2, cuBLAS -> plan, us): o_proj 9.42 -> 5.53 (1.70x) / 10.31 -> 5.74 (1.80x) / 10.19 -> 6.64 (1.54x) at 1 / 2 / 4 tokens; fused QKV 8.81 -> 6.69 (1.32x) / 8.49 -> 7.23 (1.17x), 4 tokens left to cuBLAS (1.03x); LM head 155.4 -> 142.2 (1.09x) / 156.4 -> 143.2 (1.09x), 4 tokens left to cuBLAS (1.01x).

### Tests

`pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16_skinny_gemm.py` on H200 (nightly image with #62956 and this change applied): 369 passed, 438 skipped (other architectures).

- `test_skinny_gemm_plans_are_valid` (existing, parametrized over every capability) covers the new entries.
- New `test_skinny_gemm_plans_run_and_match_linear`, parametrized over every capability table (so it also covers the SM121 entries on a GB10): calls `shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm` directly with the plan's config (a silent `F.linear` fallback cannot make it pass), asserts the kernel was compiled and compares with `F.linear`; N is capped at 4096 so the LM-head cases do not allocate 1.5 GB weights.
- `test_maybe_use_skinny_gemm` is now parametrized over the capability tables with one planned shape each.

## Details

- **4 tokens are checked inside the model.** For 4 tokens the isolated benchmark does not always predict the model. Each 4-token candidate was checked with an nsys trace of 4 concurrent requests (GEMM time per projection per decode step, cuBLAS time including its split-K reduce). Kept: Qwen3-8B o_proj 511 -> 427 us, gate/up 2071 -> 1922 us, down 1158 -> 1041 us; Qwen3-4B o_proj 387 -> 320 us, gate/up 1137 -> 1103 us; Llama-3.1-8B o_proj 452 -> 383 us; Qwen3-14B down 2077 -> 1898 us; Qwen3-32B o_proj 1811 -> 1553 us, down 4867 -> 4393 us. Dropped although they win in isolation: Llama-3.1-8B down `(4096, 14336)` (1.09x isolated, 1075 -> 1349 us in the model, made concurrency 4 3% slower) and Qwen3-14B QKV `(7168, 5120)` (1.15x isolated, 970 -> 1025 us in the model).
- **A/B testing plan changes needs a cold compile cache.** Whether a layer calls the skinny op is decided while `torch.compile` traces the model, and the plan file is not part of the compile cache key. Two servers of the same vLLM build, one with and one without a plan, can therefore load each other's cached graph. All E2E numbers above use `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`; without it, a second run of the PR arm reproduced the baseline.
- **Why the gain is largest at 1 token.** cuBLAS picks small-M `nvjet` tiles (often split-K with a separate reduce kernel) that reach 2.3-3.7 TB/s on these weights; the skinny GEMM streams the weight once with vectorized loads, reaches 3.6-4.3 TB/s, and removes the reduce kernel.
- **Startup cost.** The planned configs are compiled by the CuTe DSL warmup before CUDA graph capture: 12 compile units for Qwen3-8B (9 for Llama-3.1-8B), about 5-10 s in the server logs, once per process (no disk cache for CuTe DSL kernels today, same as the existing SM121 plans).
- **H100 / H800 / H20.** The plans are keyed by capability `(9, 0)` and were measured on an H200 only (132 SMs, 4.8 TB/s). The kernel is bandwidth bound at these sizes, so the ranking should hold on H100, but the margins were not measured there and the table header says so. I can re-measure on an H100 if a reviewer has one; otherwise the existing per-capability keying is what the SM121 table also relies on.
- **Scope.** TP=1 dense models only; TP>1 local shapes and MoE models are not covered.

---

- New `test_skinny_gemm_plans_run_and_match_linear`, parametrized over every capability table (so it also covers the SM121 entries on a GB10): calls `shape_dynamic_skinny_gemm` directly with the plan's config (a silent `F.linear` fallback cannot make it pass), asserts the kernel was compiled and compares with `F.linear`; N is capped at 4096 so the LM-head cases do not allocate 1.5 GB weights.
- `test_maybe_use_skinny_gemm` is now parametrized over the capability tables with one planned shape each.

## Details

- **4 tokens are checked inside the model.** For 4 tokens the isolated benchmark does not always predict the model. Each 4-token candidate was checked with an nsys trace of 4 concurrent requests (GEMM time per projection per decode step, cuBLAS time including its split-K reduce). Kept: Qwen3-8B o_proj 511 -> 427 us, gate/up 2071 -> 1922 us, down 1158 -> 1041 us; Qwen3-4B o_proj 387 -> 320 us, gate/up 1137 -> 1103 us; Llama-3.1-8B o_proj 452 -> 383 us; Qwen3-14B down 2077 -> 1898 us; Qwen3-32B o_proj 1811 -> 1553 us, down 4867 -> 4393 us. Dropped although they win in isolation: Llama-3.1-8B down `(4096, 14336)` (1.09x isolated, 1075 -> 1349 us in the model, made concurrency 4 3% slower) and Qwen3-14B QKV `(7168, 5120)` (1.15x isolated, 970 -> 1025 us in the model).
- **A/B testing plan changes needs a cold compile cache.** Whether a layer calls the skinny op is decided while `torch.compile` traces the model, and the plan file is not part of the compile cache key. Two servers of the same vLLM build, one with and one without a plan, can therefore load each other's cached graph. All E2E numbers above use `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`; without it, a second run of the PR arm reproduced the baseline.
- **Why the gain is largest at 1 token.** cuBLAS picks small-M `nvjet` tiles (often split-K with a separate reduce kernel) that reach 2.3-3.7 TB/s on these weights; the skinny GEMM streams the weight once with vectorized loads, reaches 3.6-4.3 TB/s, and removes the reduce kernel.
- **Startup cost.** The planned configs are compiled by the CuTe DSL warmup before CUDA graph capture: 12 compile units for Qwen3-8B (9 for Llama-3.1-8B), about 5-10 s in the server logs, once per process (no disk cache for CuTe DSL kernels today, same as the existing SM121 plans).
- **H100 / H800 / H20.** The plans are keyed by capability `(9, 0)` and were measured on an H200 only (132 SMs, 4.8 TB/s). The kernel is bandwidth bound at these sizes, so the ranking should hold on H100, but the margins were not measured there and the table header says so. I can re-measure on an H100 if a reviewer has one; otherwise the existing per-capability keying is what the SM121 table also relies on.
- **Scope.** TP=1 dense models only; TP>1 local shapes and MoE models are not covered.
